task: I'm organizing the Harbor Lights 5K, a charity run for the Eastside food pantry, happening May 17 with about 300 registered runners. Write an email to local business owners asking for a $500 sponsorship in exchange for logo placement on our shirts and a shout-out at the finish line. Keep it under 200 words and mention we raised $18,000 last year.
rewrite:
ambition:     A top fundraiser would make the email read as written to that one owner, with a merge-in first name and business name. They would frame the $500 around what it does for the Eastside pantry and for the business, instead of just listing perks. They would also end with one easy next step and a reply-by date.
agency:       The raw material is the pantry's own record of last year's $18,000 and the registration platform's count of the 300 runners. Both come from the organizer or the pantry director and are not in reach here. So the email uses only the figures you gave and invents no meals-per-dollar number.
acceleration: Use a mail merge (Google Sheets with Gmail, or Mailchimp) so each owner gets their own name and business. Use the standard sponsor-pitch order: hook, ask, what they get, one-step reply.
accuracy:     Nothing outside the model can confirm the email works, but a real send can. Send a test to yourself and one board member, then send a first batch of about 10 owners and watch the reply rate before sending the rest. A word counter confirms it stays under 200.

answers.plain:
**Subject:** Sponsor the Harbor Lights 5K, May 17

Dear [Business Owner's Name],

I'm organizing the Harbor Lights 5K, a charity run benefiting the Eastside food pantry, and I'd love for [Business Name] to be part of it.

The race takes place on May 17, with about 300 runners already registered. Last year, our community came together and raised $18,000 for neighbors who rely on the pantry. This year, we're aiming to do even more.

We're asking local businesses to become sponsors with a $500 contribution. In return, you'll receive:

- **Your logo on our official race shirts**, worn by all 300 participants and seen around the neighborhood long after race day
- **A shout-out at the finish line**, recognizing your support in front of runners, families, and spectators

Your sponsorship directly helps provide meals to families in our community, and it shows your customers that you're invested in the neighborhood.

If you're interested, just reply to this email and I'll send over the details. Shirt orders are placed soon, so a response by [date] would help us include your logo.

Thank you for considering it. I'd be grateful to have you on board.

Warm regards,
[Your Name]
[Your Title/Organization]
[Phone] | [Email]

---

That's about 190 words. Fill in the bracketed placeholders, especially the logo deadline, which should match your shirt printer's cutoff.
answers.nudge:
**Subject:** Your logo on 300 race shirts, for a good cause

Hi [Name],

I'm organizing the Harbor Lights 5K on May 17, a community run benefiting the Eastside food pantry. I'd love for [Business Name] to be part of it.

Last year, our runners and supporters raised **$18,000** for the pantry. This year, about 300 runners are registered, and we want to top that number.

For a **$500 sponsorship**, you'll receive:

- **Your logo on our official race shirt**, worn by all 300 runners on race day and around the neighborhood long after
- **A shout-out at the finish line**, in front of runners, families, and neighbors

Your support helps put food on the table for Eastside families, and it puts your business in front of the people who live and shop here.

Shirt orders go to print on **[deadline date]**, so I'd need to hear from you by then to include your logo. Could I call you this week, or would you rather I send a one-page sponsorship form?

Thank you for considering it.

Warmly,
[Your name]
[Role, Harbor Lights 5K] | [Phone] | [Email]

*(About 165 words.)*

**Notes on the choices I made:**

- **Subject line:** It leads with what the business gets. Alternatives: "Sponsor the Harbor Lights 5K: $500, 300 shirts" or "[Business Name] + the Harbor Lights 5K."
- **Shirt deadline:** A real deadline is the strongest way to prompt a reply. Work backward from your printer's turnaround and fill it in.
- **Personalization:** Add one line per recipient, such as "I'm a regular at your café" or "Your team sponsored the youth league last spring." Personalized asks usually get noticeably better responses than a blast.
- **Easy yes:** Have a one-page form or payment link ready, with logo specs (vector file, due date) and a tax-deductible receipt if the pantry is a registered nonprofit. If it is, add "your gift is tax-deductible" to the email.
- **Follow-up:** Send a short note 5 to 7 days later, something like: "Just bumping this up. We have [X] of [Y] sponsor spots left, and shirts print on [date]. Happy to answer any questions."

**One thing to check:** Today is October 26, 2026, so May 17 means 2027, which falls on a Monday. If your race is actually on a weekend, confirm the date before sending.

If you share your sponsor list or a few business types (restaurants, gyms, dental offices), I can tailor versions for each.
